Functional medicine takes a much more sane approach.

You have to dig and find the root cause of what it is that is harming you, and from there, find lifestyle solutions to adjust diet, exercise, sleep, mindset, and even supplements and drugs to actually solve the problem.
If you're frustrated with the medical system and/or the alternative healthcare system and have been bouncing around like a ping pong ball, this webinar is for you.

I've been in this industry for almost 30 years and have owned multiple clinics, sleep labs, brain labs, and multi-specialty practices. I'm also a New York Times best-selling author of eight books, and I've made over a dozen films and series, and know everybody in the functional medicine and alternative medical space.
Let me clear that up…
I know the people worth knowing.

The wellness space has now been flooded with ex-management consultants and real estate people who find some supplement or some diet that gets them better, and they suddenly become a self-proclaimed wellness expert. What helped them must certainly be good for you…
These people are giving all sorts of health advice and don't really understand what the science says because they never read the books or studies.
It's really important that you are careful where you get your information in this day and age, because it truly is the wild west.
Your average medical doctor is about 15 to 17 years behind in medical research, and your average wellness influencer has not read a single book on biology.
Strange times indeed.

Having spent 18 months making the interconnected Series and then filming several series to follow this subject matter on gut health and oral health, I have sat in the rooms where the science has been conducted and have gotten to know the smartest people in the world of medicine.
I invite you to listen to this webinar I just conducted on this topic.

body: In functional medicine, we look for the root cause.
In conventional medicine, we are looking at multiple issues that are downstream from something that is usually originating in the gut or the mouth.
We know this and have known this for at least 15 years, but conventional medicine has simply not caught up.
The key is always to look upstream and see where the inflammation or immune activation is coming from.
More often than not, that is coming from the gut lining, which is where most of our nervous system and immune system are lined up to protect us from the outside world.
The body is really good at this until it isn't, and then, when things break down, we have conditions like autoimmunity and chronic disease that are rampant in the modern world.
A lot of this comes from the foods that we're eating.
In the early days of microbiome research, myself and many other doctors were very excited about testing the microbiome and making adjustments to heal people.
This worked okay, but it certainly did not work well enough.
What we were missing was gut permeability and food sensitivities.
When I activated this in my practice, my results went through the roof, and my patients got better so much faster.
I invite you to see this special conversation I just had with James White, the CEO of KBMO Labs, who is one of the pioneers in this space.
It's important to understand that there is usually an answer out there, and nobody has taken the time to help you find it.

Swimming upstream to get to your answer oftentimes leads us to the foods we're eating, and the ones that we think are healthy are sometimes the culprit. You'll get a better sense of this when you watch the interview.

body: The supplement industry has us believing that there's a magic probiotic that'll solve all of our problems.
That is simply not true and cannot be true ever.
Why?
Because each of us has a very unique signature to our microbiome, with different species that are in excess or deficiency
A proper mapping of the microbiome goes a long way to get to this answer.
Over the years, I've had patients who have very specific species that needed to be replaced, and others that had particular species that needed specific botanicals or even antibiotics to get rid of.
The supplement guys want you to think that it's simple, so you keep buying their stuff, but ask yourself this: Why don't you feel better?
The sad truth is that it doesn't work.
What does work is swimming upstream to find the answer.

I created a very powerful tool for my doctors to be able to trust the research they were looking at. ChatGPT is now flooded with marketing information, and what it purports to be true is often gamed by the marketers. On the flip side, open evidence is where all the medical doctors are using AI to get their answers, and that subset of white males out of the Mayo Clinic were only given pharma-driven solutions.

Neither of those is a good source of truth. That's why I created my own. We uploaded all of the medical textbooks and all of the vetted studies, and then created a vetting tool for new studies that come out (so that we can actually track the good science and help our doctors make informed decisions for the patients in our programs).
I'd like to invite you to see this conversation about what it is that I created for our doctors, because we have now made it available to you.

The program is called the Upstream Navigator, and we put 2,000 people in it who are raving about how incredible it has been for them to learn about their own health and troubleshoot their problems swimming upstream to get the answers they actually deserve.

You go to the rheumatologist for your joints, the neurologist for your nerves, the cardiologist for your heart, and the psychologist for your mood.

Your internist is basically a quarterback that isn't allowed to do much and just has to send you to the specialists downstream, where you have the distinct pleasure of sitting in yet another waiting room, waiting for yet another person to spend maybe 7 minutes with you.
I can't tell you how many thousands of patients have come to me complaining about how frustrating this is.
It's dehumanizing and an incredibly disrespectful way to have someone spend their time.
It would all be worth it if you felt great, but there's the rub.

Most people are getting sicker and sicker and being put on more and more drugs despite all their efforts to go visit these “ologists.” Many of my patients have complained that they see the specialists more often than they see their loved ones.
If you can relate, you're not alone.
Here's an important conversation I have had recently with a number of our patients about this very subject.
There is a way out of this mess, but it's going to involve you.
It's time for you to take a more active role in your healing, and on the other side of this comes wisdom, knowledge, and, yes, better results.

emails.subject: Why your body won't let you sleep
emails.preview: There's a subconscious system deciding if you're safe enough to sleep. Is yours saying no?
body: I had a bout of insomnia after a trip to Europe, and it was very uncommon for me to suffer from something like this. My mind was racing, and the chatter was loud.
That sounds like a normal thing to say, but I am a monk who has studied with the Dalai Lama and spent over 40 years in meditation.
This was not mind chatter.
So, what was it?
A good functional medicine doctor and a good functional medicine patient become an investigator.
Instead of trying to shush "the baby," I decided to ask the baby what was the matter.
As I felt into it, I realized that my gut was unsettled after a summer of eating gluten and dairy in Europe.
Because I wasn't sleeping, it made sense to get up and get on PubMed.

That was a rabbit hole that took me far, far down into the depths of many studies on endotoxemia, gut permeability, immunology, and the connection of the gut-associated lymphoid tissue with anxiety, depression, and, yes, insomnia.
If you're having trouble sleeping and you've had pills thrown at you, you know that's not the solution.
Watch this talk I recently gave on the topic and see if this relates to you.
Not all insomnia comes from the gut, but at this stage in my career, I'm realizing that most of it has some cross-correlation.
It's important for you to understand where you are in this, and it's important for you to consider what I'm talking about in this video.
Enjoy,
Dr Pedram Shojai
